before.html:
Question 1
?

The quartic polynomial P(x) has roots x1=x2=x3=2, and x4=−1 and the coefficient of the quartic term is 1. Find P(x).

a
x4+3x3+8x2+12x−8
b
x4−5x3+6x2+4x−8
c
x4−3x3+6x2−12x−8
d
x4+5x3+8x2+12x−8
e
 x4−5x3+8x2+4x−8
Submit

decision.explanation: The monic polynomial is P(x)=(x-2)^3(x+1). Expanding gives (x^3-6x^2+12x-8)(x+1)=x^4-5x^3+6x^2+4x-8, which is option b.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: The quartic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=2,$ and ${x}_{4}=-1$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is $1.$ Find $P(x).$
after.worked_solution:
Since our quartic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=2,$ and ${x}_{4}=-1,$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) & =1(x-2)(x-2)(x-2)(x-(-1)) \\  & =1(x-2)(x-2)(x-2)(x+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}1(x-2)(x-2)(x-2)(x+1) & =1({x}^{2}-4x+4)({x}^{2}-x-2) \\  & =1({x}^{4}-{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-4{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+8x+4{x}^{2}-4x-8) \\  & =1({x}^{4}-5{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+4x-8) \\  & ={x}^{4}-5{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+4x-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)={x}^{4}-5{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+4x-8.$

Question 1
?

The quartic polynomial P(x) has roots x1=x2=x3=2, and x4=−1 and the coefficient of the quartic term is 1. Find P(x).

a
x4+3x3+8x2+12x−8
b
x4−5x3+6x2+4x−8
c
x4−3x3+6x2−12x−8
d
x4+5x3+8x2+12x−8
e
 x4−5x3+8x2+4x−8
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since our quartic polynomial has roots x1=x2=x3=2, and x4=−1, and the coefficient of the quartic term is a=1, we can write the polynomial as follows:

a(x−x1)(x−x2)(x−x3)(x−x4)=1(x−2)(x−2)(x−2)(x−(−1))=1(x−2)(x−2)(x−2)(x+1)

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

1(x−2)(x−2)(x−2)(x+1)=1(x2−4x+4)(x2−x−2)=1(x4−x3−2x2−4x3+4x2+8x+4x2−4x−8)=1(x4−5x3+6x2+4x−8)=x4−5x3+6x2+4x−8.

Therefore, P(x)=x4−5x3+6x2+4x−8.

content.problem: The quartic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=2,$ and ${x}_{4}=-1$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is $1.$ Find $P(x).$
content.worked_solution:
Since our quartic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=2,$ and ${x}_{4}=-1,$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) & =1(x-2)(x-2)(x-2)(x-(-1)) \\  & =1(x-2)(x-2)(x-2)(x+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}1(x-2)(x-2)(x-2)(x+1) & =1({x}^{2}-4x+4)({x}^{2}-x-2) \\  & =1({x}^{4}-{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-4{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+8x+4{x}^{2}-4x-8) \\  & =1({x}^{4}-5{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+4x-8) \\  & ={x}^{4}-5{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+4x-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)={x}^{4}-5{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+4x-8.$

after.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1,2}=\pm \text{i}$ and ${x}_{3,4}=\pm 6\text{i}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=2.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) \\  & =2(x-(-\text{i}))(x-\text{i})(x-(-6\text{i}))(x-6\text{i}) \\  & =2(x+\text{i})(x-\text{i})(x+6\text{i})(x-6\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x+\text{i})(x-\text{i})(x+6\text{i})(x-6\text{i}) & = \\ 2({x}^{2}+(\text{i}-\text{i})x-{\text{i}}^{2})({x}^{2}+(6\text{i}-6\text{i})x-36{\text{i}}^{2}) & = \\ 2({x}^{2}+1)({x}^{2}+36) & = \\ 2({x}^{4}+36{x}^{2}+{x}^{2}+36) & = \\ 2({x}^{4}+37{x}^{2}+36) & = \\ 2{x}^{4}+74{x}^{2}+72 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=2{x}^{4}+74{x}^{2}+72.$
